description:
Project Overview

The University of Luxembourg is hiring a doctoral researcher in food literacy, behaviour change and sustainable lifestyle. The project studies food practices and behaviour change in Luxembourg's foodscape - the cultural and socio-economic interrelations that shape what and how people eat - with the aim of supporting sustainable lifestyle transitions.

Your Role

  • Design and conduct qualitative research (interviews, focus groups, ethnography)
  • Apply descriptive quantitative methods to complement qualitative findings
  • Study food literacy and behaviour change in Luxembourg's socio-cultural context
  • Contribute to transformative research on agroecological and food system transitions

Funding and Employment

Employment and financial support
ComponentDetails

Eligibility and Requirements

Academic and research preparation
CriterionRequirement
Academic preparationMaster's degree in Sociology, Cultural Anthropology, Political Sciences, History and/or Geography in the field of food studies, or a related study area.
MethodsExperience and excellent skills in qualitative methods (interviews, focus groups, ethnography); good knowledge of quantitative methods (descriptive statistics).
Domain knowledgeIn-depth knowledge of Luxembourg's foodscape (cultural and socio-economic interrelations) is required; previous research on sustainable food practices is a plus.
ExperienceExperience in research project management and conduct, ideally in interdisciplinary contexts; excellent command of English plus B2-level proficiency in the language of the thesis.
